scopeNote: National Rail only. No buses, feeder services, or tram in v1 scope. Compulsory-reservation services (Caledonian Sleeper etc., if any call at northern Greater Anglia stations) are excluded by board-eligibility verdict — report did not confirm any actually call in-scope stations, treated as not-applicable rather than built and excluded. LNER at Peterborough is excluded — its board-eligibility verdict is `undecided` in the oracle report (same open question as London & South East National Rail's own LNER gap at King's Cross); per the board-eligibility rule, undecided blocks catalog inclusion, it does not default to in. Liverpool Street is NOT included in this pack — Greater Anglia services calling there are already documented as `in` in London & South East National Rail's Liverpool Street stationGroup (docs/london-se-national-rail-d1/published-network.json); do not duplicate.
notes: D1 oracle is docs/greater-anglia-d1/oracle-clash-report.md only. No product lib/cities/greater-anglia/ exists yet. Not generated from GTFS. No stopIds in this file.
Single agency (Greater Anglia), single direction model (destination + operator) at the primary hub — no two-layer hub problem like East Midlands' Nottingham Station. See direction-model-memo.md.
Modes v1: National Rail heavy rail only.

Hub lock: Norwich (NRW). Two secondary hubs: Cambridge (CBG) and Ipswich (IPS) — the oracle report supports this shape explicitly (report lines 22-24, C2/C3 point 3: both named 'Second-tier hub status', both described identically as through-routing stations on main corridors). Unlike West of England (single secondary hub, Bath Spa), the report gives no basis to flatten either Cambridge or Ipswich into a third-tier station — both have their own through-running/interchange justification (Cambridge: Thameslink cross-London; Ipswich: Great Eastern Main Line major city station with connections to London/Cambridge/Norwich/Peterborough). Kept as two secondary hubs, not one, per report evidence.

Peterborough (PBO) is explicitly NOT a hub in the report — 'through-running point, not merge... no dedicated group required within this region' (report line 25). Modelled as a flat through-running/boundary station, not a stationGroup, distinct from the Cambridge/Ipswich secondary-hub treatment. LNER verdict there is undecided/excluded; East Midlands, CrossCountry, Thameslink are in.

Colchester (COL) is 'regional hub (third tier)' per the report's own station table (line 37) — kept flat (not a secondary-hub stationGroup) since the report explicitly ranks it below Cambridge/Ipswich and gives it no through-running/boundary role of its own beyond the already-documented Liverpool Street boundary.
Ely is a regional junction with Thameslink through-running (no compulsory reservation) — kept flat, not a hub, per report's own classification (line 38: 'Regional junction station').

Station list below is the ~13 stations the report explicitly names (hub, two secondary hubs, boundary, third-tier hub, junction, branch termini, airport/commuter stations). The report itself says D1 scope is likely 30-50 of the ~170 franchise stations and explicitly defers final selection to Luke (line 43, C2/C3 point 8) — this pack does NOT invent 20-30 additional station names beyond what the report gives. Expanding the catalog to the report's suggested 30-50 range is a D2 gap for Jim to close against the Transitland GTFS feed, not something guessed here.
City lands as 'Coming Soon' (status stays planned; there is no separate coming-soon enum value in registry.js) until National Rail is unblocked, same as every other UK National Rail region this wave.

No 'lines' array is provided — National Rail has no printed route/line map to transcribe (Darwin is a per-station real-time board product), matching the East Midlands/West of England National Rail precedent. This is a flat station list with hub/secondaryHub/boundary/regional/branch classes.

printedInnerCityNames.note: Single-layer, single-primary-agency hub set — no doNotGroup needed within Norwich, Cambridge, or Ipswich (unlike Peterborough, which is a genuine multi-operator shared platform but explicitly not a merge point per the report — see hazard-pack.md H1/H4).

coverageGaps: National Rail real-time: OpenLDBWS documented and technically live, but BLOCKED at the account level (AU-registered RDM account; Tim re-registering with UK address). Not a feed problem. Do not wire DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN until it exists.

National Rail licensing: OGL 2.0 baseline permits redistribution with attribution, but the RDM Platform Agreement's language on downstream redistribution to third-party rider clients is UNCLEAR in public sources. Confidence: unclear (per oracle report License section). OPEN ITEM FOR TIM ONLY — do not resolve here.

LNER at Peterborough is `undecided` (reserved-by-default policy, one unreserved carriage maintained) — same unresolved skip risk as London & South East National Rail's own LNER gap. Excluded from this catalog per the board-eligibility rule (undecided blocks inclusion). Do not include LNER departures at Peterborough until an operator confirmation resolves the verdict — this is the same open question, not a separate one, as London & South East's.

CRS code collision found in the oracle report, not corrected here: the report's own station-code list (line 103) assigns 'LST' to Lowestoft, but 'LST' is Liverpool Street's real-world CRS and is already used as such in London & South East National Rail's built pack (docs/london-se-national-rail-d1/published-network.json, Liverpool Street stationGroup). This pack does NOT use LST for Lowestoft — Lowestoft's crs field is left null/unverified below rather than propagate a code that would collide with an already-shipped station entry. Jim must confirm Lowestoft's real CRS (believed to be LOW, not verified against GTFS here) before wiring.

Several other CRS codes in the report's list (King's Lynn given as KLY, Great Yarmouth given as YRD, Bishops Stortford given as BST) are not cross-checked against the Transitland GTFS feed or a CRS authority in this pack — carried through as reported but marked crsVerified: false. Do not treat any CRS code in this file as confirmed; Jim should verify all codes against the GTFS feed at D2.

Only the ~13 stations explicitly named in the oracle report's station table are included here. The report itself flags likely D1 scope of 30-50 stations out of ~170 franchise stations and defers final selection to Luke — this pack does not invent the remaining 17-37 station names. Expand against the Transitland GTFS feed at D2.

Peterborough is a genuine multi-operator boundary station (Greater Anglia, Thameslink, CrossCountry, East Midlands, LNER) sharing platforms with East Midlands' and a future LNER region's own D1 packs. Flagged for a multi-region ledger at D2 (cross-regional shared-platform de-dup) — not resolved in this pack, same treatment as East Midlands' Tamworth and West of England's four boundary stations.

Compulsory-reservation sleeper services (e.g. Caledonian Sleeper) possibly calling at northern Greater Anglia stations are flagged by the report as 'verify and exclude' but not confirmed either way — treated as not currently known to call any in-catalog station, not built and not excluded as a named entity. If Jim finds evidence one calls an in-catalog station at D2, it must be excluded per board-eligibility, not silently included.

nationalRailStations.note: No printed route/line map exists for National Rail in the oracle report — Darwin is a per-station real-time board, not a fixed-route product. This is a flat station list with class-based grouping, not a 'lines' array. BLOCKED pending DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN.
